comment: Integration test: drive a realistic invoice-editing session and assert the grand total (the canary) stays exactly equal to the recomputed sum at every step. A wrong total means some element interfered with another - an observer double-fired, a morph dropped a row, a binding didn't round-trip. Starts: line1 2x500=1000, line2 1x1200=1200, line3 4x75=300 => 2500. Observe fields fire on change (blur/Tab), so edits are committed with Tab.

steps.text: Reorder: move row 2 (Gadget, 1200) UP. Rows are identified by their line total (1000/1200/300) - a reorder must swap the rows, carry each row's own data with it (row-identity under reorder), leave the sum unchanged, and mirror into the rendered invoice. Then move it back DOWN to restore the pristine order for the rest of the test.

steps.name: reorder: after move-up row 0 is Gadget(1200)
reorder: row 1 is now Widget(1000) - data followed its row
reorder: rendered invoice reflects the new order (first line 1200)
reorder: move-down restored Widget(1000) to row 0

steps.text: Pick a different product in line 1 (the wonder-select). Its AjaxObserveField (observeFieldID form) must fire and refresh the rendered invoice below - changing a product, like any field, must reach the server and re-render the preview. Rendered invoice's first product cell starts 'Widget'.

steps.name: picking a product updated the rendered invoice

steps.text: Change the CUSTOMER (header). It is watched by a DESCENDANT-observing AjaxObserveField (no observeFieldID - one observer over the whole customer+tags block), distinct from the per-field observeFieldID form on the rows. Changing it must refresh the rendered invoice's Bill-to. Exercises the descendant-observe code path.

steps.name: rendered Bill-to starts as Acme Corp
descendant-observe: changing customer refreshed rendered Bill-to

steps.text: The Edit-customer modal opens purely client-side (native <dialog>, no round-trip), so its content must be kept fresh by the same customer-change update - otherwise it shows a stale customer until you open it twice. Assert the modal box (inside the still-closed dialog) already reflects the new customer.

steps.name: modal content tracks the customer change (no stale-until-reopened)

steps.text: Edit line 1 quantity 2 -> 5 (5x500=2500). Grand total should become 2500-1000+2500 = 4000. One field edit refreshes its line box AND the totals (multi-update _u=linebox-1;totalsPanel).

steps.name: line 2 was NOT disturbed by editing line 1

steps.text: Regression guard for the table-context morph bug: the edited <tr> must keep ALL its <td> cells. Multi-update of a <tr> container used to DOM-parse the fragment out of table context and drop the <td>s, collapsing the row's columns. Now the fragment html is kept as a string and morphed in the receiver's context. The count tracks the row template: currently 6 (grip, product, qty, price, lineTotal, controls) - update it when the row gains/loses a column.

steps.name: edited row kept its 6 cells (table-context morph not mangled)

steps.text: Edit line 3 unit price 75 -> 100 (4x100=400). Grand total 4000-300+400 = 4100. Proves a SECOND independent observe field works alongside the first, no cross-talk.

Add a line (default 1x100=100): grand total 4100+100 = 4200. Add-line is a multi-update refreshing the whole lines container + totals in ONE request; refreshing totalsPanel then fires its AjaxUpdateTrigger, which cascades ONE more request to summaryPanel. So 2 requests from the click itself (update + intended cascade) - NOT N-per-row. Use atLeast:2 because the page's background pollers (activity ticker every 10s, ping every 15s) may also tick inside this window - their presence is part of 'everything running together' and must not interfere with the add.

steps.name: add line fired the update + trigger cascade (not N-per-row)

steps.text: The earlier edits must SURVIVE the add-line morph: line 1 still 2500, line 3 still 400. If a morph dropped/relabelled a row, these would be wrong.

steps.name: line 1 edit survived the add-line morph
line 3 edit survived the add-line morph (no data jump)

steps.text: Remove line 2 (1200): grand total 4200-1200 = 3000. Removing a row in the MIDDLE is the classic data-jumps-lines hazard; the remaining lines must keep their own totals.

steps.name: line 1 kept its value after a middle row was removed
line 3 kept its value after a middle row was removed

steps.text: Save (AjaxSubmitButton) and confirm the form round-trips without disturbing the total.

The RENDERED invoice below must be in lockstep with the editor after all those edits: same total, and the same number of line rows (started 3, +1 add, -1 remove = 3). If a refresh missed it, the rendered copy visibly disagrees with the editor - which is the whole point of having it. The tfoot has two .num strong cells ('Total' label + amount); take the LAST.

steps.name: rendered invoice total matches the editor (3000)
rendered invoice line count matches the editor (3)

steps.text: And one more live edit propagates to BOTH the editor total and the rendered copy at once: line 1 qty 5 -> 1 (1x500=500), grand total 3000-2500+500 = 1000.

steps.name: rendered invoice updated in lockstep to 1000
